# Kinetis

> A PHP framework for persistent-worker runtimes such as FrankenPHP, which
> also runs unchanged under PHP-FPM and AWS Lambda. Attribute-driven
> routing, validation and OpenAPI; a two-tier request-scoped container;
> Fiber-based concurrency over Revolt; a native Model Context Protocol
> server.

Kinetis core ships as a single package, `kinetis/framework`, requiring PHP
8.4 or later. Narrower and optional pieces ship as separate packages,
listed under Working with data, Background work, and Integrations below.

The pages are ordered the way an application is built: start with the
tutorial, then read whichever section you have reached.

## Start here

- [Tutorial](https://kinetis.dev/docs/tutorial.html): Build a real-time application from scratch: a database, a queue, a scheduled command, and live updates over a WebSocket.
- [Core Concepts](https://kinetis.dev/docs/core-concepts.html): The runtime-agnostic Kernel, the request lifecycle, and why persistent workers change the rules.

## Building an application

- [Container](https://kinetis.dev/docs/container.html): AppScope and RequestScope, and why Kinetis bans static properties.
- [Configuration](https://kinetis.dev/docs/config.html): .env loading and typed Config access.
- [Routing & Validation](https://kinetis.dev/docs/routing-validation.html): Attribute-based routes, typed DTOs, constraint validation, and zero-config OpenAPI.
- [Middleware](https://kinetis.dev/docs/middleware.html): The PSR-15 middleware pipeline: global vs. route, plus the built-in ExceptionHandlerMiddleware/CorsMiddleware/RateLimitMiddleware.
- [Events](https://kinetis.dev/docs/events.html): A PSR-14 event dispatcher with attribute-driven listener registration, plus ShouldQueue for deferring a listener to a queue.
- [CLI](https://kinetis.dev/docs/cli.html): The kinetis CLI: built-in commands, application commands via #[Command], commands from installed packages, and restricting discovery.
- [Testing](https://kinetis.dev/docs/testing.html): TestClient, for exercising a Kernel end-to-end in a consumer's own test suite.

## Working with data

- [Persistence](https://kinetis.dev/docs/persistence.html): The native MySQL/Postgres drivers, the Redis client, and TransactionGuard's commit/rollback protocol.
- [Query Builder](https://kinetis.dev/docs/query-builder.html): kinetis/query-builder: a thin, parameterized SQL query builder — not an ORM.
- [Migrations](https://kinetis.dev/docs/migrations.html): kinetis/migrations: a thin database migration runner — raw SQL up()/down(), no schema-diffing.

## Background work

- [Queue](https://kinetis.dev/docs/queue.html): kinetis/queue: a backend-agnostic background job queue — every backend lives in its own separate package.
- [Queue (Redis)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/queue-redis.html): kinetis/queue-redis: a Redis backend for kinetis/queue's QueueInterface.
- [Queue (SQL)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/queue-sql.html): kinetis/queue-sql: a MySQL/Postgres backend for kinetis/queue's QueueInterface.
- [Queue (SQS)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/queue-sqs.html): kinetis/queue-sqs: an Amazon SQS backend for kinetis/queue's QueueInterface.
- [Queue (RabbitMQ)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/queue-rabbitmq.html): kinetis/queue-rabbitmq: a RabbitMQ backend for kinetis/queue's QueueInterface.

## Authentication and sessions

- [Authentication](https://kinetis.dev/docs/auth.html): kinetis/auth: opaque Bearer-token authentication middleware.
- [JWT Authentication](https://kinetis.dev/docs/auth-jwt.html): kinetis/auth-jwt: stateless JWT authentication (HS256/RS256), with optional per-token revocation.
- [Sessions & CSRF](https://kinetis.dev/docs/session.html): kinetis/session: cookie-backed sessions and CSRF protection — file, PSR-16 cache (Redis), and SQL storage behind one store interface.

## Runtime and performance

- [Runtime Adapters](https://kinetis.dev/docs/runtime-adapters.html): FrankenPHP, PHP-FPM, and AWS Lambda adapters, and how RuntimeDetector picks one.
- [Concurrency](https://kinetis.dev/docs/concurrency.html): Fiber-based concurrency over Revolt: concurrently(), Async\Socket, and Async\Timer.
- [Caching & AOT Compilation](https://kinetis.dev/docs/caching.html): Production-only AOT caching of routes, commands, event listeners, and validation plans, plus APP_ENV.
- [Performance tuning](https://kinetis.dev/docs/performance-tuning.html): Capacity tuning: the worker-threads x maxConnections budget, what to observe under load, and tuning by workload shape.
- [Benchmarks](https://kinetis.dev/docs/benchmarks.html): TechEmpower-style benchmark results against seven other PHP frameworks, versions tested, and results.

## Observability

- [Logging](https://kinetis.dev/docs/logging.html): PSR-3 logging: the default NullLogger, and where Kinetis logs on its own.
- [Telemetry](https://kinetis.dev/docs/telemetry.html): kinetis/telemetry: OpenTelemetry tracing — request spans, SQL/queue decorators, a traced HTTP transport, OTLP export over the Revolt-backed client.

## Integrations

- [Storage](https://kinetis.dev/docs/storage.html): kinetis/storage: file storage on League\Flysystem — a genuinely non-blocking, Amp\File-backed local adapter.
- [Storage (S3)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/storage-s3.html): kinetis/storage-s3: Amazon S3 (and S3-compatible) storage for kinetis/storage, non-blocking via kinetis/revolt-http-client.
- [Mailer](https://kinetis.dev/docs/mailer.html): kinetis/mailer: mail sending via Symfony\Component\Mailer, non-blocking via kinetis/revolt-http-client for API-based transports.
- [HTTP Client](https://kinetis.dev/docs/revolt-http-client.html): kinetis/revolt-http-client: a Revolt-native Symfony HttpClientInterface — usable standalone, no Kinetis required.
- [Search (OpenSearch)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/search-opensearch.html): kinetis/search-opensearch: OpenSearch client construction, non-blocking via kinetis/revolt-http-client.
- [AWS request signing (SigV4)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/aws-sigv4.html): kinetis/aws-sigv4: a PSR-18 client decorator signing requests with AWS Signature Version 4, non-blocking via kinetis/revolt-http-client — usable standalone.

## AI agents

- [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://kinetis.dev/docs/mcp.html): kinetis/mcp: the native Model Context Protocol server — tools, resources, stdio and HTTP transports, and protocol-era handling.

## Reference

- [Appendix: System Layout](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix.html): A dense, file-by-file reference across every namespace in core.
- [Appendix: Satellite Packages](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-packages.html): A dense, file-by-file reference across every satellite package.
- [Appendix: Continuous Integration](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-ci.html): What CI actually tests, how, and what is deliberately not covered.
- [Appendix: Contributing to Kinetis](https://kinetis.dev/docs/appendix-contributing.html): Contributing to Kinetis: the monorepo layout, dev environment setup, testing, the manifest-driven release tooling, and branching/PR/CI workflow.
